newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Ramos vows to make APEC more caring.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Ramos vows to make APEC more caring.

text.p: Issuing a strong warning against ill-directed economic growth, Philippine President Fidel Ramos pledged on Thursday to push for a kinder, gentler APEC.

"Economic growth, if we are not careful, can also cause the phenomenon of 'jobless' growth, the growing disparity between rich and poor, suppression of democratic space, decline of culture and the unleashing of environmental catastrophes," Ramos said.
Ramos, host of the fourth Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum summit, was addressing a group of environmentalists, social activists and community organisers at the presidential palace in Manila.

The activists, delegates to the most moderate of several counter-APEC conferences being held in Manila, have urged APEC's 18 members not to overlook environmental and social concerns in their pursuit of wealth.
More militant protesters have accused APEC of pushing a capitalist agenda that leaves workers vulnerable to exploitation by big business.
The moderates found a willing ear in Ramos, whose free-market policies have been credited with reviving the Philippine economy.
"Sustainable development is the bottom line in APEC, not profits," Ramos said.
He said that as this year's APEC chairman he would urge other members to formalise the role of non-government organisations as they have done with the private sector.

More than 400 private-sector executives from throughout the region meet on Friday in Manila to discuss their role as the Asia-Pacific moves towards the goal of lowering regional trade barriers by 2020.
Ramos said he would recommend to other APEC leaders at their summit in Subic Bay north of Manila that the NGOs should have a similar advisory status.

APEC groups Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.
